$comment: ★★ THE WHOLE INTEGER <-> FLOATING CONVERSION MATRIX IN ONE PROGRAM, BIT FOR BIT (P68 round 12, D-CSUBSET-INT-TO-F32-CODEGEN). 34 cells: {signed, unsigned} {8, 16, 32, 64}-bit integer to `float` and to `double`, `float` and `double` to {signed, unsigned} {8, 16, 32, 64}-bit integer, and `float` -> `double` / `double` -> `float`. Each cell's values cross a `volatile` before a plain C cast and its result's BIT PATTERN is compared with the correctly rounded (to nearest, ties to even, one rounding) or truncated value the lane's conversion-matrix generator computed in exact arithmetic; float -> integer inputs are all in range. Exit 42 = every cell right, else the number of the first wrong cell (the list in main.c). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24 before the change, one program per cell through the shipped CLI on x86_64 PE, x86_64 ELF and arm64 ELF, debug and release: the 8 integer -> `float` cells were REFUSED everywhere (`only an F64 (double) destination`) and the other 26 ran right. gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (-O0/-O2), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 under qemu (-O0/-O2), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 (-O0/-O2) and MSVC 19.51 (/Od, /O2) run this program to 42. It is the one witness that carries every cell to the Mac, where only the example runners reach. The `release` arm pins the same file through the shipped release pipeline.
